s: Martha affirms she knows Lazarus will rise in the resurrection at the last day. Jesus responds that he himself is the resurrection and the life, and that whoever believes in him will live even if he dies and will never die. He then demonstrates this by calling Lazarus out of the tomb.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: In Chapter 12, six days before the Passover, Jesus comes to Bethany, where Mary anoints his feet with costly nard ointment at a supper attended by Martha and Lazarus. Judas Iscariot objects, and Jesus defends Mary, saying she kept it for the day of his burial. Crowds come to see Jesus and Lazarus, the chief priests plot to kill Lazarus, and Jesus enters Jerusalem on a young donkey to cries of 'Hosanna!' from a multitude carrying palm branches. When some Greeks ask to see him, Jesus says the time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, speaks of the grain of wheat dying, and prays 'Father, glorify your name,' after which a voice from the sky answers. The chapter ends with Jesus' warning to walk in the light, the narrator's explanation of the people's unbelief through Isaiah, and Jesus' declaration that he came as light to save the world and speaks only what the Father commanded.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: Jesus comes to Bethany six days before the Passover, defends Mary's anointing as preparation for his burial, and enters Jerusalem sitting on a young donkey as the crowd hails him as King of Israel. He announces that the time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified, says that when lifted up from the earth he will draw all people to himself, and then hides from the crowd. He declares that he came as a light to save rather than judge the world and speaks only what the Father commanded.

l: Lazarus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: Lazarus, whom Jesus raised from the dead, sits at the table with Jesus at the supper in Bethany. Crowds come partly to see him, and the chief priests conspire to put him to death too because many of the Jews believed in Jesus on account of him.

l: Mary, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: Mary takes a pound of very precious pure nard ointment, anoints Jesus' feet, and wipes them with her hair, filling the house with fragrance. Jesus defends her against Judas, saying she has kept it for the day of his burial.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: Judas Iscariot, Simon's son and one of the disciples who would betray Jesus, objects that the ointment should have been sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor. The text says he did not care for the poor but was a thief who held the money box and used to steal from it.

l: ointment (Mary's ointment), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: The ointment is a pound of pure nard, very precious, which Mary pours on Jesus' feet and which fills the house with fragrance. Judas says it could have been sold for three hundred denarii, while Jesus says she kept it for the day of his burial.

l: crowd (at the feast), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: A large crowd of the Jews comes to Bethany to see Jesus and Lazarus, and a great multitude at the feast greets Jesus in Jerusalem with palm branches and cries of 'Hosanna!' The multitude that had been with him when he raised Lazarus testifies about it, and they go to meet him because they heard of the sign. Later some of the multitude hear the voice from the sky, think it thunder or an angel, and question how the Christ can be 'lifted up'.

l: God, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: The Father sent Jesus and gave him a commandment about what to say and speak, and that commandment is eternal life. In response to Jesus' prayer 'Father, glorify your name,' a voice from the sky says it has both glorified the name and will glorify it again. Jesus says that to believe in or see him is to believe in or see the one who sent him, and that the Father will honor anyone who serves Jesus.

l: Jesus' raising of Lazarus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: The raising of Lazarus from the dead is recalled as a sign that draws crowds to Bethany and to meet Jesus. The multitude who were present testify about it, the Pharisees lament that the world has gone after Jesus, and the chief priests plot to kill Lazarus because many believed on account of him.

l: Jesus' death and glorification, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: Jesus links his coming death to his burial, to the time for the Son of Man to be glorified, and to the image of a grain of wheat that falls into the earth and dies to bear much fruit. He says his soul is troubled but he came to this time for this cause, and that being lifted up from the earth will draw all people to himself. The narrator says this signified what kind of death he should die, and that the disciples later remembered these things when Jesus was glorified.

l: belief and unbelief in Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 12
s: Many of the Jews believe in Jesus because of Lazarus, while the multitude welcomes him as King, but despite his many signs others do not believe, which the narrator ties to Isaiah's words about blinded eyes and hardened hearts. Many rulers believe but do not confess it for fear of the Pharisees and being put out of the synagogue, because they loved men's praise more than God's. Jesus urges belief in the light so people may become children of light, and says that one who rejects him will be judged by the word he spoke on the last day.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: Before the Passover, Jesus, knowing his time to return to the Father had come, rises from supper and washes his disciples' feet. Simon Peter first objects, then asks to be washed more fully, and Jesus tells him that the disciples are clean but not all of them, since he knows who will betray him. Jesus explains the washing as an example for the disciples to follow, then announces that one of them will betray him. He identifies Judas Iscariot by giving him a dipped piece of bread, Satan enters Judas, and Judas goes out into the night. Jesus then speaks of glorification, gives a new commandment that the disciples love one another, and tells Peter that Peter cannot follow him now and will deny him three times before the rooster crows.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: Jesus, knowing his time had come to depart to the Father, lays aside his outer garments, washes the disciples' feet, and tells them to do likewise as an example. He announces that one of them will betray him, identifies Judas by giving him dipped bread, and tells him to do quickly what he does. He then speaks of glorification, gives a new commandment of love, and predicts that Peter will deny him three times.

l: Simon Peter, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: Simon Peter objects to Jesus washing his feet, then, when told he would have no part with Jesus otherwise, asks to be washed on his hands and head as well. He beckons the disciple leaning on Jesus to ask who the betrayer is. He asks where Jesus is going, says he will lay down his life for him, and is told he will deny Jesus three times before the rooster crows.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, is described as having the devil put betrayal into his heart and as holding the money box. Jesus gives him the dipped piece of bread, Satan enters him, and Jesus tells him, "What you do, do quickly." He takes the morsel and goes out immediately, and it was night.

l: disciples (Jesus' disciples), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: The disciples have their feet washed by Jesus and are told they are clean, but not all of them. They look at one another, perplexed, when Jesus says one will betray him, and nobody at the table knows why he tells Judas to act quickly. Jesus commands them to love one another so that everyone will know they are his disciples.

l: God, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: God is the Father to whom Jesus is going and who has given all things into Jesus' hands. Jesus says God has been glorified in the Son of Man and will glorify him in himself immediately. He also says that whoever receives him receives the one who sent him.

l: foot washing, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: Jesus washes the disciples' feet and wipes them with a towel wrapped around his waist. He presents it as an example, saying that if the Lord and Teacher has washed their feet, they ought to wash one another's feet. Peter's resistance prompts Jesus to say that without being washed, one has no part with him.

l: supper, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: The supper is the setting before the Passover feast in which Jesus rises, washes feet, and later dips bread for Judas. At the table the disciple whom Jesus loved leans against his chest. Some of those present think Jesus' words to Judas concern buying things for the feast or giving to the poor.

l: betrayal of Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: The devil has already put betrayal into the heart of Judas, and Jesus knows who will betray him. Jesus cites Scripture about one who eats bread with him lifting his heel against him, then announces that one of the disciples will betray him. He identifies Judas with the dipped bread, and Judas leaves.

l: new commandment of love, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: Jesus gives a new commandment that the disciples love one another just as he has loved them. He says that by this love everyone will know they are his disciples.

l: Peter's denial prediction, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 13
s: When Peter says he will lay down his life for Jesus, Jesus answers by asking whether he will and tells him the rooster won't crow until Peter has denied him three times. This follows Jesus' statement that Peter cannot follow him now but will follow afterwards.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: In this chapter Jesus comforts his disciples, telling them not to be troubled and that he is going to his Father's house to prepare a place for them and will come again to receive them. Thomas asks how they can know the way, and Jesus answers that he is the way, the truth, and the life and that no one comes to the Father except through him. Philip asks to be shown the Father, and Jesus replies that whoever has seen him has seen the Father, who lives in him and does his works. Jesus promises answered prayer in his name, ties love for him to keeping his commandments, and promises the Father will send another Counselor, the Spirit of truth, who will teach them and remind them of his words. He leaves his peace with them, explains that the Father is greater than he, says the prince of the world is coming, and ends by telling them to arise and go from there.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Jesus comforts his disciples, saying he is going to prepare a place for them and will come again to receive them. He declares himself the way, the truth, and the life, says whoever has seen him has seen the Father, and promises that the Father will send the Counselor. He gives his peace, states that the Father is greater than he, and ends by telling the disciples to arise and leave.

l: God the Father, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: The Father is said to dwell in Jesus and to do his works through him, and the words Jesus speaks are the Father's. He will give another Counselor in answer to Jesus' prayer, will love those who love Jesus, and will come with Jesus to make a home with them. Jesus says the Father is greater than he and that he has commanded Jesus what to do.

l: Thomas, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Thomas tells Jesus that the disciples do not know where he is going and asks how they can know the way. His question leads Jesus to say he is the way, the truth, and the life.

l: Philip, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Philip asks Jesus to show them the Father, saying that would be enough for them. Jesus responds by asking whether Philip still does not know him after so long, and says that whoever has seen him has seen the Father.

l: Holy Spirit, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: The Spirit is described as the Counselor and the Spirit of truth, whom the Father will send in Jesus' name to be with the disciples forever. The world cannot receive him because it neither sees nor knows him, but the disciples know him, since he lives with them and will be in them. He will teach them all things and remind them of all that Jesus said.

l: disciples (Jesus' disciples), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: The disciples are told not to let their hearts be troubled and are promised a place prepared for them, the Counselor, and Jesus' peace. Thomas and Philip show they do not yet understand where Jesus is going or who the Father is, and Judas (not Iscariot) asks why Jesus will reveal himself to them and not to the world. Jesus tells them that those who love him keep his word, that they will see him while the world does not, and that he will not leave them orphans.

l: world, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: The world cannot receive the Spirit of truth because it does not see or know him. Jesus says the world will see him no more after a little while, and that he will reveal himself to his followers and not to the world. He also says the prince of the world is coming but has nothing in him, and that the world is meant to know that he loves the Father.

l: Father's house, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Jesus says the Father's house has many homes. He is going there to prepare a place for his disciples so that they may be where he is.

l: the way (path to the Father), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Jesus tells the disciples they know where he goes and the way, and when Thomas objects, Jesus says he himself is the way, the truth, and the life. He states that no one comes to the Father except through him.

l: commandments, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Jesus says that if the disciples love him they will keep his commandments, and that the one who has and keeps them is the one who loves him. Those who love him will be loved by the Father and by Jesus, who will reveal himself to them. Whoever does not love him does not keep his words, which are the Father's.

l: Jesus's departure and return ('a little while'), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 14
s: Jesus tells the disciples he is going to his Father to prepare a place and that he will come again to receive them. He says he will come back to them and will not leave them orphans, and that after a little while the world will no longer see him but they will. He says he has told them beforehand so that they may believe when it happens.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: In Chapter 15, Jesus describes himself as the true vine, his Father as the farmer, and his followers as branches who must remain in him to bear fruit. Branches that bear no fruit are taken away and burned, while fruitful ones are pruned to bear more. Jesus commands his followers to remain in his love and to love one another as he has loved them, calling them friends because he has made known to them everything he heard from his Father. He warns that the world will hate and persecute them as it hated him, because they are not of the world and the world does not know the one who sent him. He promises that the Counselor, the Spirit of truth, will testify about him, and that the disciples will also testify because they have been with him from the beginning.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: Jesus calls himself the true vine and says apart from him his followers can do nothing. He commands them to remain in his love and love one another, says he has loved them as the Father loved him, and calls them friends, having chosen and appointed them. He tells them the world will hate them as it hated him, and says he will send the Counselor from the Father.

l: God, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: The Father is the farmer of the vine, who takes away fruitless branches and prunes fruitful ones. He is glorified when the disciples bear much fruit, loves Jesus, and gives whatever the disciples ask in Jesus' name. Jesus says he kept the Father's commandments, heard everything from him, and will send the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father.

l: disciples (Jesus' disciples), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: The disciples are the branches, already pruned clean by Jesus' word, and are told to remain in him, keep his commandments, and love one another. They are called friends rather than servants, were chosen and appointed by Jesus to bear lasting fruit, and are warned of the world's hatred and persecution. They will testify about Jesus because they have been with him from the beginning.

l: world, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: The world hates Jesus and, because they are not of the world, hates the disciples too. Jesus says it would love its own, that it persecutes because it does not know the one who sent him, and that it has no excuse for its sin since it has seen his works and hated both him and the Father. This fulfills the written saying, 'They hated me without a cause.'

l: fruit (fruit-bearing), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: Fruit is what branches bear only by remaining in the vine; fruitless branches are removed and burned, and fruitful ones are pruned to bear more. Bearing much fruit glorifies the Father and shows the disciples to be Jesus' disciples. Jesus appointed them so that their fruit should remain.

l: love, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 15
s: Jesus says he loves the disciples as the Father has loved him, and tells them to remain in his love by keeping his commandments. His commandment is that they love one another as he loved them, and he says there is no greater love than laying down one's life for friends.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: In Chapter 16, Jesus tells his disciples that they will be put out of the synagogues and killed by people who do not know the Father or him, and he explains that he is telling them this so they will remember and not stumble. He says it is to their advantage that he goes away, because then he will send the Counselor, the Spirit of truth, who will convict the world about sin, righteousness, and judgment and guide the disciples into all truth. Jesus speaks of 'a little while' when they will not see him and then will see him again, and the confused disciples are told their sorrow will turn into joy, like a woman's anguish in childbirth giving way to joy. He promises that they may ask the Father in his name and that the Father himself loves them. When the disciples claim they now believe because he speaks plainly, Jesus warns that they will be scattered and leave him alone, yet he is not alone because the Father is with him, and he tells them to cheer up because he has overcome the world.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: Jesus warns his disciples of coming persecution, says it is to their advantage that he goes away so he can send the Counselor, and speaks of going to the Father. He tells them that they will be scattered and leave him alone, yet he is not alone because the Father is with him, and he declares that he has overcome the world.

l: disciples (Jesus' disciples), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: The disciples are told they will be expelled from synagogues and killed, and that sorrow has filled their hearts. They are puzzled by 'a little while,' then say they believe because he speaks plainly, but Jesus says they will be scattered and leave him alone. They are promised that their sorrow will become joy, that they may ask the Father in Jesus's name, and that in him they may have peace.

l: God, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: The Father is the one who sent Jesus, and Jesus says he is going to him. The Father himself loves the disciples because they have loved Jesus and believed he came from God, will give whatever they ask in Jesus's name, and is with Jesus so that he is not alone. All that the Father has is Jesus's.

l: Holy Spirit, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: Jesus says the Counselor will not come unless he goes away, and that he will send him. When he comes he will convict the world about sin, righteousness, and judgment, guide the disciples into all truth, speak only what he hears, declare things that are coming, and glorify Jesus by taking from what is Jesus's and declaring it to them.

l: world, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: The world is to be convicted by the Counselor about sin because they don't believe in Jesus, about righteousness because Jesus goes to the Father, and about judgment because the prince of this world has been judged. It will rejoice while the disciples weep and lament, and Jesus says he has overcome it, though in it the disciples have trouble.

l: Jesus's departure and return ('a little while'), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: Jesus says that in a little while the disciples will not see him, and again in a little while they will see him, linked to his going to the Father. The disciples do not understand the phrase, and Jesus, perceiving their wish to ask, explains it through their coming sorrow and joy. He later says he came from the Father into the world and now leaves the world to go to the Father.

l: sorrow turned to joy, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 16
s: Jesus tells the disciples that they will weep and lament while the world rejoices, but their sorrow will be turned into joy. He compares it to a woman who forgets her anguish after giving birth because of joy that a child is born, and promises that he will see them again, their hearts will rejoice, and no one will take their joy away. He adds that asking in his name will make their joy full.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: In Chapter 17, Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and prays to the Father. He asks to be glorified so that he may glorify the Father, and says he has finished the work given to him. He prays for the disciples whom the Father gave him out of the world, asking that the Father keep them from the evil one, sanctify them in truth, and make them one. He then extends the prayer to those who will believe through the disciples' word, asking that they be one in the Father and Son so that the world may believe he was sent. He closes by desiring that they be with him to see his glory, and says he has made the Father's name known and will keep doing so, so that the Father's love may be in them.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: Jesus prays to the Father, asking to be glorified with the glory he had before the world existed, and says he has glorified the Father on earth and accomplished the work given him. He reports that he revealed the Father's name, gave the disciples the Father's words, and kept them, losing only the son of destruction. He sanctifies himself for the disciples' sake and prays for them and for future believers.

l: God, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: The Father is addressed as Holy and Righteous Father, the only true God. He gave Jesus authority over all flesh and gave Jesus the disciples out of the world. Jesus asks him to glorify the Son, keep the disciples in his name and from the evil one, and sanctify them in his truth, and says he loved Jesus before the foundation of the world.

l: disciples (those given to Jesus by the Father), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: The disciples were the Father's, given to Jesus out of the world, and they have kept the Father's word. They received Jesus' words, knew for sure that he came from the Father, and believed he was sent. Jesus prays that they be kept, be one, be sanctified in truth, have his joy made full, and be with him to see his glory; he sent them into the world as the Father sent him.

l: world, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: The world is the realm from which the disciples were given and into which they are sent. It hated the disciples because they are not of the world, and it has not known the Father. Jesus does not pray for it, but he asks that the disciples' unity lead the world to believe and know that the Father sent him and loved them.

l: future believers (those who will believe through the disciples' word), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: Jesus prays specifically for those who will believe in him through the disciples' word, extending his prayer beyond the disciples. He asks that they all be one, as the Father and Son are one, and be one in them, so that the world may believe that the Father sent him.

l: eternal life, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: Eternal life is defined as knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent. Jesus says that, having been given authority over all flesh, he will give eternal life to all whom the Father has given him.

l: glory, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: Jesus asks the Father to glorify him so that he may glorify the Father, and to restore the glory he had with the Father before the world existed. He says he is glorified in the disciples and has given them the glory the Father gave him. He desires that they see his glory, which the Father gave him because he loved him before the foundation of the world.

l: unity (oneness of believers with Father and Son), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 17
s: Jesus prays that the disciples be one as he and the Father are one, with the Father in him and he in them. He extends this to all future believers, that they be one in the Father and Son and be perfected into one. The purpose is that the world may believe and know that the Father sent him and loved them as he loved Jesus.

l: The Gospel According to John, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: Jesus goes with his disciples to a garden across the Kidron, where Judas arrives with a detachment of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees. Jesus identifies himself, the group falls to the ground, and he asks that his disciples be let go; Peter strikes Malchus, the high priest's servant, and is told to put away his sword. Jesus is bound and taken to Annas, then Caiaphas, while Peter denies being a disciple three times before the rooster crows. The Jews bring Jesus to Pilate at the Praetorium, where Pilate questions him about kingship and truth, finds no basis for a charge, and offers to release him, but the crowd demands Barabbas instead.

l: Jesus, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: Jesus goes to the garden, identifies himself to those seeking him, and asks that his disciples be allowed to go. He rebukes Peter for using the sword, is bound, questioned by the high priest, slapped by an officer, and sent to Caiaphas and then Pilate. Before Pilate he says his Kingdom is not of this world and that he came to testify to the truth.

l: Judas Iscariot, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: Judas, who betrayed Jesus, knew the garden because Jesus often met there with his disciples. He led a detachment of soldiers and officers there with lanterns, torches, and weapons, and stood with them when Jesus identified himself.

l: Simon Peter, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: Peter draws a sword and cuts off the right ear of Malchus, the high priest's servant, and Jesus tells him to sheathe it. He follows Jesus to the high priest's court, where he is brought in by another disciple and denies being a disciple three times, the last followed immediately by a rooster crowing.

l: Pilate, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: Pilate goes out to the Jews who will not enter the Praetorium, tells them to judge Jesus by their own law, and learns they cannot put anyone to death. He questions Jesus about being king, declares he finds no basis for a charge, and offers to release Jesus under the Passover custom, but the crowd chooses Barabbas.

l: Caiaphas, The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: Caiaphas is identified as the high priest that year and father-in-law of Annas's... correction: son-in-law of Annas, and as the one who advised that it was expedient for one man to perish for the people. Annas sends the bound Jesus to him, and from his house Jesus is led to the Praetorium.

l: detachment of soldiers and officers (sent by the chief priests and Pharisees), The Gospel According to John, Chapter 18
s: The detachment, led by Judas, comes with lanterns, torches, and weapons, and falls backward to the ground when Jesus says "I am he." Together with its commanding officer and the officers, it seizes Jesus and binds him.
